title: Inside GovDash’s Advanced Proposal Content Generation System
summary: Meet advanced content generation in GovDash Proposal. Proposal drafting now runs on a new system that plans, researches, drafts, and checks its work. Dash adapts to each section’s needs, revisits weak results, and flags missing evidence.
body_markdown:
A strong technical approach connects the solicitation’s requirements, your writing plan, and evidence of what your company can deliver, all within the page limit.


GovDash’s new content generation system gives Dash a more deliberate way to build that response. Dash plans each section, researches supporting material, and checks its work as it drafts. Your team gets an editable first draft with inline citations and flagged evidence gaps.


### **What’s new**


A technical approach, a past performance table, and an executive summary require different strategies. Dash now adapts its approach to each, drawing on the solicitation, your company knowledge in GovDash, and the capture work already completed on the opportunity.


Previously, content generation followed a predefined sequence. Now, Dash selects actions from a plan, evaluates each result, and decides what to do next.


If a search returns too little evidence, Dash will search again with different instructions. Sections that need improvement return for additional planning, research, and drafting. If a later step fails, completed sections are preserved.


Your team starts review with the supporting sources in place and missing evidence identified.


In testing across multiple different proposal types, advanced generation filled in about **2x as many sections** as our previous approach, covered more than **4x as many solicitation obligations** , and stayed within every page limit. For proposal managers, that means fewer sections to write from scratch, fewer missed requirements, and more time to strengthen the response before color review.


### **How the system works**


The workflow connects strategy, storyboarding, research, drafting, and review. Dash uses an existing win strategy when one is available, plans the claims each section needs to make, and selects supporting evidence.


*The flow illustrates the work involved in developing a proposal. Dash selects and revisits actions based on each section’s needs; not every section requires the same fixed sequence.*


During drafting, Dash reads the outline and related sections, searches supporting material, and checks the draft. Quality checks can send work back for revision. Sections needing deeper rework return to planning and research.


Before Dash accepts a section, it runs **22 automated checks covering citations, unsupported claims, placeholders, repetition, copied solicitation text, and page limits** . On a large operations and maintenance test proposal, 31 of 37 sections went back for revision at least once before they passed.


After drafting the sections, Dash checks the proposal for repeated arguments and overlapping content. It writes the cover letter and executive summary last so they reflect the completed response.


### **Evidence you can review, gaps you can resolve**


Inline citations connect claims to their source documents, so reviewers can check the evidence behind the response. When supporting material is missing, Dash flags the claim for review.


That traceability supports the work Miranda Brunett at Vision IT describes:


> *“GovDash turns our past performance into competitive narratives. It draws on what we’ve actually delivered and frames it around what the evaluator is looking for: relevance, outcomes, and discriminators.”* **Miranda Brunett, Vision IT**


In a nine-proposal test, the previous system left 9 to 12 placeholders for the team to complete in each proposal. The new system produced drafts with no remaining placeholders in seven of the nine proposals. When it couldn’t find evidence to support a claim, it flagged that claim for review.


Your team can focus review on the claims that need attention, with supporting sources available to check.


### **Built for the demands of government proposals**


ChatGPT and Claude can help teams research and write. Government proposals also need a process to trace claims to evidence and check the response against specific solicitation obligations.


Advanced content generation builds proposal-specific tools and checks into that process. Dash works from requirements assigned to each section, retrieves past performance and other company evidence, and checks drafts for issues such as missing requirement details, citation problems, and repeated content.


Proposal task GovDash Proposal ChatGPT, Claude, General LLM


Requirement coverage Maps solicitation obligations to sections to guide drafting and review. Can analyze requirements; your team sets up section mapping and coverage review.

Citations Inline citations with automated checks for citation formatting and references. Can provide source citations; proposal-specific validation depends on your workflow.

*Comparison covers general-purpose use. ChatGPT and Claude can also be extended with custom tools and integrations.*


Your team gets these capabilities within the proposal workflow, with less to configure and maintain through prompts. Reviewers can use the requirements and sources alongside the draft to assess coverage, substantiate claims, and validate commitments before submission.


### **Keep the proposal moving from outline to review**


Advanced content generation builds on the rest of GovDash Proposal, where your team manages solicitation requirements, compliance matrices, outlines, and section writing plans. Together, these give reviewers a shared foundation for checking coverage and strengthening the response.


> *“GovDash has been a great tool to get us from the PWS to a strong first draft. It helps us structure our responses quickly and in tune with our template.”- **Dominic Codd, OFS***


When the work moves into Microsoft Word, the Dash Word add-in brings your AI teammate into the document. **Dash stays connected to the solicitation requirements in GovDash Proposal** , so as your team edits, it can reference requirements and check the draft against them without leaving Word.


### **From company knowledge to a stronger proposal**


The new content system brings proposal drafting onto the same Dash infrastructure that powers Agents across GovDash. It connects the work of building a response to the company knowledge and pursuit context your team has already developed.


Dash handles the research, drafting, and checks, giving your experts more room to validate the approach, sharpen discriminators, and make a persuasive case for your company.
